name: Shuo Zhang
description: Shuo Zhang is a PhD candidate in Transportation Systems at New York University. His research uses human-in-the-loop simulation to address out-of-distribution and safety-critical scenarios in autonomous driving and road safety. He previously earned his master's degree at UCLA.

experience.summary: Human-in-the-loop simulation, human-factors analysis, and learning-based driving models.
bullets: Built a dual-user VR–CARLA platform for multimodal data collection on driver–worker interactions in safety-critical, out-of-distribution driving scenarios.
Analyzed driving behavior, gaze, physiological signals, and questionnaires; developed ego-vehicle trajectory prediction models using multimodal work-zone driving data.
Developing a co-simulation testbed for reinforcement learning-based motion planning, including closed-loop traffic, a PPO baseline, reward design, and generalization tests.

experience.summary: Built real-time LiDAR diagnostics and automated hardware validation.
bullets: Developed two Python/C tools for real-time LiDAR health monitoring of temperature, voltage, and data rate, replacing Wireshark-based diagnostics.
Automated thermal and vibration testing using USB relays, Arduino, and Raspberry Pi, following ISO and GM standards.
Designed and conducted LiDAR validation experiments, including optical-module checks, image analysis, burn-in quality control, and data visualization.
